destination.question: How do matter exchange, curvature coupling, gauge/form interactions or modified expansion laws change scalar cosmological histories and acceleration?

sources.title: Limits from Weak Gravity Conjecture on Dark Energy Models

evidence.text: A decaying vacuum with physical EoS −1 cannot be separately conserved. The model supplies an interaction with dust and asks whether an effective canonical scalar description can satisfy the excursion criterion.

sources.title: Anisotropic $2$-form dark energy

evidence.text: Can a scalar coupled to a two-form support late-time acceleration with wDE close to −1 despite a steep exponential potential, while generating surviving anisotropy through a viable radiation–matter–dark-energy sequence?

sources.title: Swampland conjecture in $f(R)$ gravity by the Noether Symmetry Approach

evidence.text: How do power-law curvature corrections affect scalar criteria and cosmological behavior? The paper treats epsilon as a theory parameter and separately expands near the General Relativity value epsilon=0.

sources.title: Topological Eternal Hilltop Inflation and the Swampland Criteria

evidence.text: Can a modified expansion law increase Hubble damping without requiring a conventionally flat potential? The imported brane cosmology changes the relation between potential energy and H while retaining the scalar damping equation.

sources.title: The Effective Potential Originating from Swampland and the Non-trivial Brans-Dicke Coupling

evidence.text: Why include curvature-scalar coupling in an auxiliary description of late-time acceleration?

sources.title: Higuchi Bound on Slow Roll Inflation and the Swampland

evidence.text: A homogeneous scalar drives the g-sector expansion while a second metric changes the gravitational response through y=b/a. The relevant background dynamics combine a scalar equation, one Friedmann equation, and an algebraic interaction constraint.

sources.title: Swampland conjectures and single-field inflation in nonstandard cosmological scenarios

evidence.text: The reviewed alternatives motivate examining whether modified expansion alone can ease the tension in a canonical supercooled single-field model.

sources.title: Axion inflation in the strong-backreaction regime: decay of the Anber-Sorbo solution

evidence.text: Is the Anber–Sorbo (AS) solution stable when evolution starts directly in strong gauge-field backreaction, and how do its growth rates, survival time and subsequent dynamics change when the Hubble rate evolves?

sources.title: Scalar field dynamics in non-minimally coupled theories via the Noether symmetry and the Eisenhart-Duval lift

evidence.text: Which scalar potentials, conserved quantities and cosmological solutions follow from Noether symmetry in non-minimally coupled scalar gravity, and how does the Eisenhart-Duval lift express these dynamics geometrically?

sources.title: Non-minimally coupled scalar field dark sector of the Universe: in-depth (Einstein frame) case study

evidence.text: Which cosmological histories, stability properties and acceleration regimes arise for five Einstein-frame scalar–dust interaction models, including negative potentials, and how do coupling and CPL-motivated initial conditions change their evolution?

sources.title: Non-minimal coupling, exponential potentials and the w < -1 regime of dark energy

evidence.text: Can a scalar with ordinary kinetic sign, exponential potential, and nonminimal gravitational coupling have stable expanding solutions that pass through w < -1 and approach de Sitter space for large sets of initial conditions?

sources.title: Scaling solutions in general nonminimal coupling theories

evidence.text: Can general nonminimal scalar–gravity couplings produce scaling attractors with appreciable scalar energy and present acceleration, with dynamics determined by the relation between coupling and potential rather than their individual functional forms?

sources.title: Interactions in scalar field cosmology

evidence.text: Can energy exchange between an exponential-potential scalar field and matter change cosmological attractors, permit inflation without eliminating matter, and produce oscillatory approach to late-time solutions relevant to inflation or accelerated expansion?

sources.title: Inflation and quintessence with nonminimal coupling

evidence.text: How does nonminimal scalar–curvature coupling change cosmic acceleration for a given potential, and when are slow-roll approximations and conformal transformation methods justified?

sources.title: Cosmological scaling solutions of nonminimally coupled scalar fields

evidence.text: How does nonminimal scalar–curvature coupling affect the existence, equation of state, and stability of cosmological scaling solutions for inverse power-law and exponential scalar potentials?

sources.title: Limits from Weak Gravity Conjecture on Dark Energy Models

evidence.text: Absorb the phenomenological interaction into an effective vacuum pressure, reconstruct a canonical background scalar from that effective stress tensor, and integrate its redshift derivative. Changing the decay law requires solving the interaction and background again.

sources.title: Anisotropic $2$-form dark energy

evidence.text: Find fixed points algebraically and assess homogeneous linear stability using eigenvalues of a five-by-five Jacobian. Numerically integrate cosmological trajectories and compare their evolution with fixed-point predictions and approximate observational shear criteria.

sources.title: Swampland conjecture in $f(R)$ gravity by the Noether Symmetry Approach

evidence.text: Reduce the covariant theory to FRW minisuperspace, vary a and R, and impose the energy constraint. The paper fixes cosmic-time lapse before its classical symmetry analysis.

sources.title: Topological Eternal Hilltop Inflation and the Swampland Criteria

evidence.text: For each mu, choose an appropriate endpoint, solve the corrected e-fold equation, and evaluate conventional tilt and tensor ratio. The source omits amplitude normalization. Printed inconsistencies and possible earlier epsilon termination prevent certifying the observable curve from this route.

sources.title: The Effective Potential Originating from Swampland and the Non-trivial Brans-Dicke Coupling

evidence.text: Close an underdetermined cosmological model with one phenomenological relation, then integrate its background. The alternatives are not ranked by a small parameter, error estimate, or expansion order.

sources.title: Higuchi Bound on Slow Roll Inflation and the Swampland

evidence.text: The paper expands the scalar energy, solves the metric-ratio constraint order by order, inserts the result into the generalized mass, and tests W>0. A consistent implementation must expand the Friedmann response and the mass response at the same order.

sources.title: Revisiting Scalar Tensor inflation by swampland criteria and Reheating

evidence.text: Can a scalar-dependent gravitational coupling accommodate slow-roll inflation, the observed scalar/tensor spectra, and the paper's swampland cuts? The study also asks which effective reheating equations of state give positive, relatively short expansion histories.

sources.title: Swampland conjecture in $f(R)$ gravity by the Noether Symmetry Approach

evidence.text: Can symmetry-selected f(R) gravity connect a conjectural quantum-gravity origin with primordial and present cosmic acceleration? The paper investigates scale-factor duality together with bounds on an effective scalar potential.

sources.title: Anisotropic dark energy from string compactifications

evidence.text: Can a string-inspired modulus–axion system coupled to a pure U(1) vector produce stable late-time acceleration with small anisotropy despite a steep scalar potential, and are the required couplings compatible with the compactification structures considered?

sources.title: Long-lived SEC violation via DM/DE couplings

evidence.text: Can a dark-matter/dark-energy coupling sustain acceleration despite an overly steep scalar potential, and what limits its duration or permits evolution toward controlled string asymptotics?

sources.title: Coupled quintessence

evidence.text: Which accelerated cosmological trajectories exist for a scalar with an exponential potential and explicit linear matter coupling, and how do their CMB and matter perturbations constrain the coupling?

sources.title: Horndeski gravity in the swampland

evidence.text: This ansatz tests whether a potential-driven scalar with cubic and quartic derivative interactions and exponential gravitational coupling can generate viable acceleration. It is the concrete model underlying the reported slope constraints.

sources.title: k-Essence, superluminal propagation, causality and emergent geometry

evidence.text: How do scalar perturbations on a prescribed expanding background compare with perturbations that include the gravitational response of a scalar-driven universe? The comparison uses conformal time, a homogeneous background field, and distinct test-field and cosmological canonical variables.

sources.title: Late time acceleration in a slow moving galileon field

evidence.text: Can a slow-moving slotheon scalar with a potential produce viable late-time cosmic acceleration, and what do background evolution, matter growth and the historical observational data imply for its parameters?

sources.title: Effective Field Theory of Cosmic Acceleration: an implementation in CAMB

evidence.text: How can the EFT of cosmic acceleration be implemented in CAMB to predict linear cosmological observables for mapped single-scalar theories and parametrized EFT models, while retaining scalar time evolution and checking theoretical viability?

sources.title: Constraints on field flows of quintessence dark energy

evidence.text: How can a homogeneous canonical scalar produce the observed late-time expansion while remaining consistent with measured cosmological distances and Hubble rates?

sources.title: Consistency of Cubic Galileon Cosmology: Model-Independent Bounds from Background Expansion and Perturbative Analyses

evidence.text: Can derivative interactions reconcile an order-one potential slope with observed late-time expansion, and does that same model survive a linear-growth comparison? The paper tests these questions together with conjectural restrictions on field excursions and future accelerated expansion.

sources.title: On energy and particle production in cosmology: the particular case of the gravitino

evidence.text: How do particle states obtained by diagonalizing the instantaneous Hamiltonian of canonically normalized fields differ from states diagonalizing the stress-tensor energy operator in expanding FLRW spacetime, particularly for longitudinal gravitinos and their goldstino description?

sources.title: Cosmology with a primordial scaling field

evidence.text: Can a primordial, persistently subdominant exponential scalar field improve SCDM structure formation without introducing a scalar energy scale characteristic of recent epochs, while satisfying early-universe and historical observational constraints?

sources.title: k-Essence, superluminal propagation, causality and emergent geometry

evidence.text: Match the principal and first-derivative parts of the scalar operator to an emergent covariant d'Alembertian. Solve for its conformal normalization using the determinant and derivative-Hessian identities.

sources.title: Late time acceleration in a slow moving galileon field

evidence.text: Minimize a joint χ² from growth, 580 UNION2.1 supernovae, BAO distance ratios and a CMB shift parameter; eliminate the supernova nuisance parameter μ0. The reported scan varies β from −0.3 to 1 and Ωm0 from 0.2 to 0.35.

sources.title: Effective Field Theory of Cosmic Acceleration: an implementation in CAMB

evidence.text: Pure EFT fixes the expansion history and Ω, reconstructs c and Λ, and independently specifies perturbation-only coefficients. Mapping EFT solves a chosen model's background and reconstructs its EFT coefficients through matching.

sources.title: Constraints on field flows of quintessence dark energy

evidence.text: Integrate the dimensionless scalar in ln a, using algebraic density and equation-of-state relations to remove explicit H_0 and potential normalization. Applicability requires a matter-plus-scalar background and resolution of the printed coefficient discrepancy.

sources.title: Consistency of Cubic Galileon Cosmology: Model-Independent Bounds from Background Expansion and Perturbative Analyses

evidence.text: Integrate the scale-independent growing-mode equation using H, Ωm and Geff/G, then differentiate lnD+ and form ln f/lnΩm. This operation separates actual model growth from an approximate γ inferred only from the background.

sources.title: On energy and particle production in cosmology: the particular case of the gravitino

evidence.text: Perform time-dependent canonical field rescalings, solve nondynamical constraints and decompose helicities. Quantize and diagonalize both quadratic operators through Bogolyubov transformations, then compose the transformations to compare their vacua. Bosonic coefficients obey |α|²−|β|²=1; fermionic coefficients obey |α|²+|β|²=1.

sources.title: Cosmological constraints on tachyon matter

evidence.text: Under what initial conditions can rolling tachyon matter have an acceptable density today without premature domination, and can it cluster gravitationally enough to serve as cosmological dark matter?

sources.title: Revisiting Scalar Tensor inflation by swampland criteria and Reheating

evidence.text: Can a scalar-dependent gravitational coupling accommodate slow-roll inflation, the observed scalar/tensor spectra, and the paper's swampland cuts? The study also asks which effective reheating equations of state give positive, relatively short expansion histories.

sources.title: Multifield dark energy: Interplay between curved field space and curved spacetime

evidence.text: Can spatial curvature and nongeodesic modulus–axion motion jointly permit observationally viable late-time acceleration on steep exponential potentials?

sources.title: Loop quantum gravity corrections to gravitational wave dispersion

evidence.text: The setting isolates the two tensor polarizations of metric perturbations on a spatially flat expanding universe. Ashtekar variables make their Hamiltonian evolution accessible to corrections motivated by a loop quantization.

sources.title: k - inflation

evidence.text: Can nonquadratic scalar kinetic terms, without a potential, generate expanding Einstein-frame inflation with decreasing curvature, acceptable scalar perturbations and a graceful transition to a radiation-dominated universe?

sources.title: Assisted inflation

evidence.text: Can multiple scalar fields with individually steep exponential potentials cooperate through cosmic expansion to produce inflation, and what scaling attractor and curvature-perturbation spectrum result when their slopes differ?

sources.title: Cosmological dynamics of multifield dark energy

evidence.text: Can rapidly turning scalar trajectories produce late-time acceleration on steep potentials for a broad set of initial conditions, while remaining theoretically viable and distinguishable from ΛCDM?

sources.title: Trans-Planckian Censorship and the Swampland

evidence.text: What quantum uncertainty applies to the scalar assigned to an entire Hubble patch? Appendix C treats that scalar as a normalized spatial average on a Cauchy surface, with RMS field displacement and RMS velocity.

sources.title: Machine Learning and cosmographic reconstructions of quintessence and the Swampland conjectures

evidence.text: Which canonical scalar potential and kinetic energy reproduce an observed expansion history in a matter-plus-scalar GR background?

sources.title: A species scale-driven breakdown of effective field theory in time-dependent string backgrounds

evidence.text: When does a decreasing species scale overtake initially infrared cosmological perturbations, invalidating gravitational EFT, and what does this imply for asymptotic string cosmologies and the duration of accelerated expansion?

sources.title: Catastrophic production of slow gravitinos

evidence.text: How does cosmological expansion modify the constrained dynamics of a massive vector-spinor? The external FRW background permits a homogeneous mass history while preserving the spatial symmetries needed to label modes by comoving momentum.

sources.title: Prospects and problems of tachyon matter cosmology

evidence.text: Can late-stage rolling tachyon condensates provide cosmologically useful negative-pressure matter or cold dark matter once field and gravitational instabilities are included?

sources.title: Coupled quintessence

evidence.text: Which accelerated cosmological trajectories exist for a scalar with an exponential potential and explicit linear matter coupling, and how do their CMB and matter perturbations constrain the coupling?

sources.title: The zoo plot meets the swampland: mutual (in)consistency of single-field inflation, string conjectures, and cosmological data

evidence.text: How does a nearly flat canonical scalar potential generate approximately constant expansion, and which dimensionless derivatives control this approximation?

sources.title: Accelerating cosmology from Λ < 0 gravitational effective field theory

evidence.text: Can negative-Λ gravitational EFTs support observationally plausible accelerated expansion while retaining time-symmetric bang/crunch solutions with asymptotically AdS Euclidean continuations, and can the required scalar potentials arise from a superpotential?
